scenes.text: Will AI take my job? It's the question everyone is asking. [1] The honest answer is, AI changes tasks first, and jobs second. [2] Let's look at what's really happening to work, and how to stay ahead.
[1] Here's the key idea. [2] A job is a bundle of tasks. [3] AI is good at some tasks, like drafting, summarising, and sorting. [4] So most jobs change, rather than disappear completely.

data.definition: Every job is a bundle of tasks. AI automates some tasks, which reshapes the job more often than it removes it.

scenes.text: There are two ways AI affects work. [1] Automation, where AI does a task instead of a person, like sorting invoices. [2] Augmentation, where AI helps a person do more, like a doctor using AI to read scans faster.

[1] Some tasks are more exposed than others. [2] Routine writing and data entry, high exposure. [3] Coding and analysis, heavily assisted. [4] Hands-on work, like plumbing or nursing care, lower exposure. [5] And jobs built on trust and relationships, like teaching and sales, change, but stay human.

AI also creates new jobs. [1] The World Economic Forum's 2025 report expects about 170 million jobs created, and 92 million displaced, by 2030. [2] New roles include AI trainers, evaluators, and AI engineers. [3] And every field now needs people who can use AI well.

So how do you stay ahead? [1] Learn to use AI tools in your own field, like you're doing right now. [2] Build human strengths, like judgement, communication, and creativity. [3] And keep learning. Skills now change every few years.
Here's a common myth. [1] People say AI will replace everyone. [2] A more accurate saying is, AI won't replace you, but a person using AI well might. The advantage goes to people who learn it early.

data.fact: AI won't replace you, but a person using AI well might.
